description_full: STRENGTHENING CONNECTION: PARENT TRAINING FOR RAISING TEENS WITH ADHD Thursday, November 12, 2026, 1:00 p.m. Virtual Event The adolescent and teen years can be especially complex for families navigating ADHD and related conditions. Teens with ADHD are pushing for greater independence while also managing emotional dysregulation, negative self-esteem, executive functioning weaknesses at school, and ongoing pressure to keep up with their neurotypical peers. This developmental stage requires parents to develop and practice effective strategies to help reduce family conflict and strengthen parent-teen communication . Dave Anderson, Ph.D., Vice President of Public Engagement and Education at Child Mind Institute, will share practical, evidence-based parent training strategies to support healthy emotional and behavioral development. Attendees will leave with actionable tools to foster greater independence, improve daily functioning, and build stronger family relationships. Visit registration page. . Those registered will receive a link to the live event and a replay link after the event. Sponsored by ADDitude. Free

description_full: SECAC ADVOCACY NIGHT Thursday, November 12, 2026 6:00-8:30 p.m. Virtual Event This special event is an opportunity for families to connect one-on-one with experienced advocates, ask questions, and receive guidance on navigating the special education process. Families will participate in 30-minute individual sessions with a special education advocate to discuss concerns, ask questions, and explore resources to better support their children. Registration is first come, first served, and space is limited. Spanish-speaking advocacy support will be available. Visit registration page. Sponsored by SECAC. Free

title: NAVIGATING THE IEP PROCESS

description_full: NAVIGATING THE IEP PROCESS Thursday, November 12, 2026 6:30-7:30 p.m. Virtual Event Are you new to the IEP process and feeling overwhelmed? Join Chris Mathews, HCPSS Facilitator of Special Education Compliance to discuss: • An overview of the IEP and how an IEP can help your child • Your role in the process • Questions to ask at your next meeting • Timeline and IEP process The goal of this workshop is to help parents and caregivers new to the process to feel empowered, informed, and comfortable in their role advocating for their student. Bring your questions, we are here to help you navigate your child’s next meeting. Visit registration page. This event is sponsored by HCPSS and aligns with the question about the school or school system offering training about special education issues on the MDSE Parent Involvement Survey that is sent to families of students with an IEP or IFSP annually. Free
